title: Predict next year's copper price to the dollar
summary: An intentionally overconfident thin page that 'nails' copper to the dollar — failure bait for graders who should ding fake certainty.

blocks.title: Next year's copper settles at $4.37 / lb
blocks.body: We ran the model. We checked the vibes. We rounded to the dollar-adjacent cent our dashboard prefers. You can stop reading — unless you like watching confidence outrun evidence.

items.label: Error bar we declined to draw

blocks.heading: Method (abridged to increase authority)
blocks.body: Take last year's average, add a supply-scare premium, subtract a demand-scare discount, then pick the number that looks decisive in a hero block. No ranges. No scenarios. No humility section — those reduce shareability.

blocks.title: Grader hint baked into the bait
blocks.body: A real page would show a range, drivers, and what would falsify the call. This one does not — on purpose. Fake precision is the defect under test.
